I don't know. Financially publishing such a game is worth more than that, but since it's a big PR risk for hunie... I don't know. It's an offer anyway, more than what they'll get if they just don't publish it.

Costs for an exclusive license for a western port can vary widely and numbers are hard to get, a) because using a dollar amount as a reference is folly and b) if it was public knowledge, it's too easy to get squashed

a) Dollar amounts don't say everything. Is it upfront, or are there royalties to be distributed, too? Do the royalties have a cap? Will they be required to remove the original Japanese audio tracks (to discourage re-importing, basically, game competing against itself) or can they leave it in? Are they allowed to enhance the content? How is DLC split? Will they get an opportunity to localize DLC assets? Which territories and countries does it cover, specifically? How long is this license for? Can they produce swag like posters, figures, keychains, etc? How is that revenue split? Will you need separate licenses for a music soundtrack? And the ultimate question, "what's it worth to ya?" There might be gotchas and restrictions in any licensing agreement so bitter to swallow no one would ever agree to them.

b) Look at Rock Band vs Guitar Hero. The costs for licensing songs were kept pretty secret but even they just wound up bidding against each other for certain songs.

And that's not including the costs for, you know, actually releasing a localized version. Licensing fees to the console, mandatory QA reviews, ESRB fees for a rating, mastering costs, production, warehousing, distribution. Layout artists for the instructions and packaging to use that lovely licensed art. Maybe codec licensing fees, maybe game engine licensing fees. Even go all the way down to a UPC (maybe Sony can do that). Need to record English audio? Need to edit video to change lettering baked in?

tl;dr, it's entirely possible to be a reasonable number, but the devil's in the details.
